name: doc-digest
desc: Free, open-source document summarizer for Windows — long PDFs into digests and Q&A with local LLMs. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Long-document handling** — map-reduce passes digest 500-page PDFs that would blow a single context window
✅ **Chapter outline** — structure rebuilt as a collapsible outline before the summary is written
✅ **Key point cards** — decisions, numbers and named entities pulled out as scannable cards
✅ **Q&A with citations** — ask about the document and every answer links to the page it came from
✅ **Batch digests** — a folder of reports each summarized into its own markdown file
✅ **Quote finder** — search the original text for a phrase and jump to the passage
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, models downloaded separately, offline after that, MIT
compare: | Price | **Free, MIT** | Paid tiers | Free web | Your weekend |
| Documents stay local | **Yes** | Upload | Upload | Yes
| Works on 500-page files | **Yes** | Partial | Partial | Yes slowly
| Batch folder digests | **Yes** | One by one | No | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Browser | Browser | N/A
faqQ: summarize long PDFs offline without uploading confidential documents?
faqA: Cloud PDF chat tools want the full document uploaded, which rules out contracts and internal reports. doc-digest processes long files locally in passes, builds an outline and answers questions with page citations. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, and can digest a whole folder while you do something else.
s1: Dark reader (#121417, amber #D97706): outline tree left with 24 chapters, digest pane right with key point cards, citation chips linking to page numbers.
s2: Q&A panel: question about payment terms typed in the bar, answer with two highlighted page links beneath, confidence note chip on the row.
s3: Batch view: 14 report files with digest status and lengths, per-file markdown checkmarks, folder output path chip, progress at 9 of 14.
